topic:student-visa:tb_test:2026.verified_value: Nigeria is on the GOV.UK list of countries where you need a TB test: if you are coming to the UK for 6 months or more and have lived in Nigeria for 6 months or more (within the last 6 months), you need a TB test (a chest x-ray); the certificate is valid for 6 months from the x-ray and goes with your visa application
topic:student-visa:tb_test:2026.page: https://www.gov.uk/tb-test-visa/countries-where-you-need-a-tb-test-to-enter-the-uk, read 2026-10-05 via page-excerpts run 37313413454, sha256 ee9c0afab2d598fc; https://www.gov.uk/tb-test-visa sha256 c7150f96ca766c28
topic:student-visa:tb_test:2026.quote: [country list] ... Niger (get tested in another country) ⏎ Nigeria ⏎ North Korea ... [tb-test-visa] You'll need to have a tuberculosis (TB) test if all of the following are true: ⏎ you're coming to the UK for 6 months or more ⏎ you've lived in any of these listed countries for 6 months or more ⏎ you were living there (or another listed country) within the last 6 months ... You'll be given a chest x-ray to test for TB ... a certificate which is valid for 6 months from the date of your x-ray. Include this certificate with your UK visa application.

topic:gmc-registration:f1_visa_route:202.verified_value: Foundation doctors who need a visa can be sponsored for a Skilled Worker visa after allocation to a programme (a Certificate of Sponsorship is arranged by the national sponsorship teams, not the UKFPO); a Graduate visa needs no sponsorship. Right to work does not have to be shown when applying
topic:gmc-registration:f1_visa_route:202.note: Corrects the earlier wording (Health and Care Worker visa sponsored by the employing trust).
